Where is the wedding going to be?
I don’t know, again. Great question.
Will I be invited to the wedding?
Honestly, if you’re reading this at this point, probably. But then again, I don’t know.
When is the RSVP deadline?
Please RSVP by DATE to help us finalize the guest count. Please understand that RSVPs beyond this date cannot be accommodated.
Can I take photos or videos during the ceremony?
No! We are asking all of our guests to power off their devices and keep them out of sight during the ceremony. This will help our professional team of photographer and videographers to achieve the nicest unobstructed views of the ceremony. This will also allow you to enjoy the moment in your memories alongside of us.
Can I bring a plus one?
Please check your invitation for details.
Are kids welcome?
As much as we’d love to share our evening with your little ones, we will be keeping this celebration to adults only. Thank you for understanding.
What time should we arrive?
Please refer to the schedule. We will be doing our very best to stay on schedule, so please help us by arriving 15-20 minutes before the scheduled time.
Where should I park?
Parking info, I guess?
What should I wear?
Dress code is semi formal. Elegant and chic attire; think suits, knee+ length dresses, dress shoes, heels or dressy flats. Please wear approriate clothing for the occasion.

articles.contents:
Victoria falls honeymoon fund




Our favourite memories together involve travelling, whether from roadtrips, foodtrips, to flying across the globe. We chose Victoria falls as a honeymoon destination for a few reasons:
We love water, and waterfalls. Fallingwater is a big part of our memories together
Mountains and surreal terrains is a close second to beautiful bodies of water
What a perfect excuse to go somewhere further away than ever before, than getting lost on our honeymoon

articles.title: My Adventure Buddy
articles.contents:
How did you two meet?
Alejandro: We ended up playing on the same soccer team by chance. And we started talking during the social events of the team and then we really enjoyed each other’s company to the point that we planned a trip to new york, shortly after we met. The rest is history.Monique: I moved to Pittsburgh ‘after’ COVID in Spring 2021, in doing so I was trying to meet new people and make friends; I joined two different soccer teams. The second team was the friendlier of the two, we ended up all hanging after our games. We started talking and learned we shared an interest in road trips. And that’s where it all started. Nearly two years of friendship and adventures later, we chose to start our romantic relationship together, and here we are!

How did the proposal happen?
Alejandro: It happened during a trip because that’s what we like to do together.
I planned a surprise vacation to a special location for the two of us. I chose the place because it has both a beach element and a little chapel that looked very cute that I thought she would like. On the day of we woke up and I was very insistent on going to this beach and struggling to find reasons to go to the beach without raising suspicion. It was a little bit more walking than I thought once we got there. As we were approaching the chapel, I knew my sister was nearby and when we were in her camera’s range, and front of the chapel’s stairs, a fisherman caught a giant Octopus! Monique was very distracted by the Octopus, meanwhile I am trying to regain her attention and struggling to remember my speech. I started telling Monique that I love her a lot, that I really like her and that I have a very important question. And right before I said anything she asked, woah, what’s going on. And then I got down on one knee and taking Monique’s hand and asked her if she wanted to marry me. We both got emotional and…she said yes!
Got up gave her a big hug and told her everything was being recorded.
Monique: On day 3 of a surprise birthday trip to Portugal Alejandro wanted to go explore a beautiful beach just south of Porto. It was a little chilly and till 8am so I was a little confused why we would rush to the beach before grabbing at least a little picnic. We arrived at a still sleepy practically empty beach with gorgeous sand, and rocks on the Atlantic ocean. Just off in the distance there happened to be a chapel, and I enthusiastically said that I would like to go see it! Upon approaching the chapel Alejandro got more nervous, and me more concerned for the very nervous Alejandro. Until he suddenly stopped. Right in front of the steps of the chapel on the rock, he asked me to marry him. ( I hadn’t noticed that he stopped because a fisherman had just pulled AN ENTIRE OCTOPUS OUT OF THE OCEAN, and that was my first time seeing that!!).

Who asked whom out first?
Alejandro: She asked me out first. We were in Toronto, and we wanted to go out to eat at Pai’s. We sat at the bar and we started talking very honestly to each other. And next thing I remember is her saying that the ball was in my court. I wanted to make sure we knew what were signing up for, and it went way better than I thought. Look at us now!MT: I’m not entirely sure. Looking back it’s hard to tell when our ‘first date’ really was.

What is our favorite trait about your partner?
Alejandro: I really like how intentional and thoughtful you are about everything you do and say.
Monique: He’s my kind of weird! More earnestly, he’s incredibly thoughtful of, and committed to, the people he loves.

Name one quirky trait/memory about your partner.
Alejandro: Recognizing how she reacts to her pet peeves. I can now differentiate those smaller reactions and that means a lot. For example, on the volleyball, I don’t wanna write it right now because I’m shy.
Monique: He’s goofy…lol…There are so many memories, across so many continents. I think my favourite memory is of the feeling of coming home from work and spending a cozy evening together. A more specific memory is of driving home from a roadtrip at midnight still a few hours to go while blasting the radio singing our hearts out to our roadtrip playlist.

What is our favorite travel memory together?
Alejo: We went to this beach in the outer banks, and we wanted to go stargazing. We drove there, and it was quiet, we were the only ones there. We just laid down on the beach being amazed by how beautiful the sky looked.
Monique: That time we never actually made it to inca inca beach in Colombia. In short, we spent an afternoon on a sailboat cruise, and got soaking wet from the rainsotmr that had suddenly arrived; we absolutely froze. The goal of the sail boat was to arrive to inca inca, and we still yearn for the day we will arrive to see this mystical beach on the Colombian coast near Santa Marta.

I met Monique on the first day of grade 10, she was the first person to talk to me in school as a new student when I knew no one. I didn’t realize that our paths crossing that day would result in over 17 years of lore. Monique has always been an incredibly inspiring, kind hearted, and hilarious, brilliant mind for as long as I’ve known her. She always encouraged me to be brave and reach for my goals, from teaching me to play bass in music class when I was 16 to making me introduce myself to a band when I was 22, that I now work my dream job for. We witnessed each other change and persevere and chase our dreams. I couldn’t be more proud of who she is and I’m honoured to still be a part of her journey to this day. I’m so grateful to know you and to call you my precious friend.
